people.name: Rob Jetten
people.role: Prime Minister of the Netherlands and Minister of General Affairs since 23 February 2026, leading a minority cabinet of D66, VVD and CDA; D66 party leader since August 2023

D66.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
D66.position: Governs with VVD and CDA under a coalition agreement promising 'more control and reduced inflow' together with decent reception. Its election programme supports the EU Pact, keeps the Spreidingswet, and wants a statutory children's pardon and work and language lessons from day one. In the House D66 voted against repealing the Spreidingswet (23 June 2026). In the Senate the D66 group reached a 'negative judgement' on the Schoof-cabinet bills, mainly over criminalising illegal stay, and Senator Dittrich voted against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet; the group voted for the Pact implementation act.

D66.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
D66.position: Supports taxing actual returns and voted for both the February 2026 bill and the November amending bill. NOS reports D66 leans towards a yearly growth tax and opposed funding a capital gains tax at the expense of lower incomes; MP Oosterhuis called the minister's funding a fairly creative reading of the budget rules. D66 made the Tax Plan deal with CDA, PRO and Volt that adds a 38.5% top rate.

D66.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
D66.position: D66 campaigned on building ten new cities and on phasing out the mortgage interest deduction over at least 15 years. In December 2025 D66 and CDA jointly proposed a gradual phase-out once compensation through income tax is possible. In the coalition agreement D66 accepted that the tax treatment of the home stays unchanged; on 12 May 2026 it nevertheless voted for a motion to reverse the automatic increase in the deduction rate.

D66.title: Tax burden on income and work
D66.position: Governing party (prime minister Rob Jetten). Its manifesto says allowances are too complex and that taxes hit workers harder than the wealthy, and proposes replacing allowances step by step with an individual basic amount. In November 2026 D66, with CDA, agreed the tax-shift amendment with PRO and Volt and voted for the amended 2027 Tax Plan.

VVD.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
VVD.position: Wants inflow of all forms of migration to fall and a new system in which all asylum applications are handled outside Europe and refugees come by invitation only, which it says could mean years without admitting asylum seekers. Until then it wants the strictest possible policy: closed reception and faster removal for nuisance-causing applicants, return hubs, and a legal ban on priority for status holders in social housing. The VVD voted against repealing the Spreidingswet on 23 June 2026 as a coalition party; its Senate group supported the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet and the Pact implementation act.

VVD.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
VVD.position: Wants a capital gains tax, in which tax is paid only on realised returns, as fast as possible and opposes higher taxes on wealth. Voted for the February 2026 bill; VVD senators later threatened to vote against it, and VVD minister Heinen initiated the amending bill. Voted for the amending bill and for JA21's rejected amendment to cut the rate by 3 points, and against the 2027 Tax Plan after the two-rate amendment was adopted.

VVD.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
VVD.position: VVD wants 30 large new residential districts, fewer rules and shorter objection procedures, more affordable owner-occupied homes and a 'radical' loosening of rules on the rental market to attract investors. It wants to keep the mortgage interest deduction: its leader Yesilgöz said in September 2025 the party would not join a cabinet that changes it, and the coalition agreement keeps it unchanged.

VVD.title: Tax burden on income and work
VVD.position: Governing party. Its manifesto wants a simpler tax system in which work pays, an end to what it calls excessive levelling through allowances, deductions and credits, eventually no allowance system, and no tax increases on savings (box 3), enterprise (box 2) or inheritance and gifts. The VVD rejected the D66/CDA deal with PRO and Volt and voted against the 2027 Tax Plan on 12 November 2026 while remaining in the coalition.

PRO.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
PRO.position: The merged GroenLinks-PvdA voted against repealing the Spreidingswet in the House (23 June 2026). In the Senate, where the group still sits as GroenLinks-PvdA, it requested roll-call votes and voted against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet and against the Pact implementation act; Senator Karimi said the bills intrude deeply on asylum seekers' rights and that limiting family reunification is legally vulnerable. With the ChristenUnie, PRO obtained a House majority for a motion to examine state-owned property as long-term reception so that children do not end up in emergency shelter.

PRO.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
PRO.position: Voted for the February 2026 bill and against the amending bill, which it considers unnecessary, rushed and unfunded. Wants wealthy people rather than workers to pay for any shortfall. Together with Volt it proposed the amendment creating a 38.5% box 3 top rate, adopted on 12 November 2026 with D66 and CDA support.

PRO.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
PRO.position: PRO (the merged GroenLinks-PvdA; the sources cited still use the name GroenLinks-PvdA) wants to phase out the mortgage interest deduction in 8 to 12 years and use the proceeds to build affordable homes. Its motion to reverse the automatic increase in the deduction rate was adopted on 12 May 2026. In the Senate GroenLinks-PvdA voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

PRO.title: Tax burden on income and work
PRO.position: The GL-PvdA manifesto (the merged party now sits as PRO) says tax on work goes down and taxes on income from wealth go up, wants to make allowances unnecessary step by step, and would phase out the expat ruling. PRO leader Jesse Klaver co-submitted the amendment that lowers the first-bracket rate and adds a box 3 top rate, and PRO voted for the amended Tax Plan.

PVV.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
PVV.position: Wants an immediate asylum stop and repeal of the Spreidingswet, and tabled motions for both in the Senate (rejected 21 April 2026) and the House (rejected 23 June 2026, 45-100 on a roll call it requested). The amendment that criminalised illegal stay in the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet came from PVV MP Vondeling. Its Senate group called the Schoof-cabinet bills 'a step in the right direction', voted for them and for the Pact implementation act. In 2025 a PVV amendment banning any priority for status holders in social housing won a House majority.

PVV.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
PVV.position: Voted against both the February 2026 bill and the amending bill. NOS lists the PVV among parties favouring a full capital gains tax; MP Vlottes opposed taxing unrealised gains, criticised the speed of the process and called the funding phantom cover. The PVV asked in writing whether the cabinet should resign over the handling of the file.

PVV.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
PVV.position: The 2025 manifesto has a chapter 'Homes for the Dutch': a 10% cut in social rents with compensation for housing associations, keeping the mortgage interest deduction, a national crisis plan for housebuilding and no priority for status holders in social housing under any circumstances. A PVV amendment banning such priority was adopted by the House in July 2025 and later removed through the novelle; in the Senate the PVV voted against the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting and for the novelle.

PVV.title: Tax burden on income and work
PVV.position: The PVV manifesto concentrates on VAT and excise rather than income tax rates: VAT on energy from 21% to 9%, no VAT on groceries, no fuel excise increase, 21% VAT on art and culture, and an end to the expat ruling. On 12 November 2026 PVV members Vlottes and Wilders tabled a motion of no confidence in the cabinet during the Tax Plan votes. The PVV is not among the groups reported as supporting the Tax Plan.

CDA.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
CDA.position: Coalition party that supplies the Minister of Asylum and Migration, Bart van den Brink. Supports the EU Pact and voted for its implementation act, and voted against repealing the Spreidingswet. In the Senate the CDA called the criminalisation of illegal stay 'a very nasty political quickie' and voted against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet once the novelle exempting helpers had been rejected, while asking for new proposals on declaring people undesirable, ending penalty payments and criminalising non-cooperation with return.

CDA.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
CDA.position: States it favours a full capital gains tax. Voted for the February 2026 bill; NOS reported that CDA senators later threatened to vote against it. Voted for the amending bill while questioning the funding and the process, and joined D66, PRO and Volt in the Tax Plan deal that raises tax on wealth. MP Inge van Dijk asked for a reform of the whole tax and benefits system rather than box 3 alone.

CDA.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
CDA.position: CDA's 2025 manifesto proposed phasing out the mortgage interest deduction over thirty years and using the money to lower income tax. In the coalition agreement it accepted leaving the deduction unchanged, and on 12 May 2026 it voted for the motion to reverse the automatic increase. In the Senate CDA voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

CDA.title: Tax burden on income and work
CDA.position: Governing party. Its manifesto proposes phasing out mortgage interest relief step by step while lowering income tax by the same amount, a labour tax credit applied per hour worked, automatic payment of allowances, fewer income-dependent schemes to lower the marginal burden, and keeping the expat ruling. The coalition agreement left the mortgage interest deduction unchanged. CDA made the November 2026 deal with PRO and Volt together with D66 and voted for the Tax Plan.

JA21.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
JA21.position: Wants a sharp reduction of all immigration, a Danish-style model with reception in the region or partner countries, criminalisation of illegal stay and active removal. MP Ceulemans is first signatory of the initiative bill to repeal the Spreidingswet and said the party also wants to end asylum reception altogether. JA21 voted for all motions to repeal the law (23 June 2026); its Senate group supported the Schoof-cabinet bills and the Pact implementation act.

JA21.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
JA21.position: Wants tax only on what a person has actually earned, levied when the gain is realised. Voted against the February 2026 bill and for the amending bill. Wants crypto and precious metals included as soon as possible. Its amendment to lower the box 3 rate by 3 percentage points was rejected. NOS reported in September 2026 that JA21 made a budget deal conditional on a quick capital gains tax.

JA21.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
JA21.position: JA21 wants large-scale building inside and outside existing towns, faster procedures, exempting housebuilding from nitrogen restrictions, repeal of the Wet betaalbare huur and no automatic priority for status holders. NOS noted in 2025 that its manifesto did not mention the mortgage interest deduction. In the Senate JA21 voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

JA21.title: Tax burden on income and work
JA21.position: JA21's manifesto proposes a new, strongly simplified tax system to lower the marginal burden, abolishing allowances and tax credits in favour of a simple system of 'toelagen', and abolishing box 2 by taxing substantial shareholdings in box 3. According to Taxlive, JA21 worked together with SGP and BBB during the Tax Plan debate and set far-reaching conditions for support; IamExpat reports the three threatened to vote against the box 3 reform if the wealth-tax changes were adopted.

Groep Markuszower.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
Groep Markuszower.position: The group that split from the PVV in January 2026 voted for all motions to repeal the Spreidingswet and to end compulsion on municipalities (23 June 2026). MP Markuszower, after whom the group is named, argues that an asylum stop alone is not enough and asked the minister for a plan with a timetable for large-scale return of people without lawful residence and for systematic withdrawal of permits obtained with invented stories.

Groep Markuszower.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
Groep Markuszower.position: Voted against the February 2026 bill and for the amending bill. It was one of two groups, with FVD, that voted for abolishing box 3 through a 0% rate, and it supported the rejected amendment to lower the rate by 3 percentage points.

Groep Markuszower.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
Groep Markuszower.position: No housing programme, position page or housing statement of this House group was found in the sources consulted for this file.

Groep Markuszower.title: Tax burden on income and work
Groep Markuszower.position: The group has no 2025 manifesto of its own (it split from the PVV in January 2026). On the 2027 Tax Plan, Markuszower submitted amendments to apply the full inflation correction in 2027 and to raise the labour tax credit, and a motion to abolish the freedom contribution for businesses as well.

FVD.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
FVD.position: Wants to stop asylum reception in the Netherlands, dismantle COA, accept applications only at consulates in conflict regions, criminalise illegal stay and leave treaties such as Schengen and the UN Refugee Convention. FVD co-signed the initiative bill to repeal the Spreidingswet. In the Senate it voted for all three Schoof-cabinet bills, calling the novelle 'bad' but honouring an agreement, and voted against the Pact implementation act because it wants the Netherlands itself to decide who enters.

FVD.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
FVD.position: Opposes taxing savings and investments as such and wants box 3 abolished. Voted against both the February 2026 bill and the amending bill. Its amendment to set the rate at 0% was rejected; it also proposed keeping the shareholder borrowing cap at EUR 500,000, which was rejected.

FVD.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
FVD.position: FVD wants 100,000 homes a year, the scrapping of climate and nitrogen rules for building, repeal of the Wet betaalbare huur, a limited social-rent sector with priority for Dutch citizens over status holders, and a mortgage interest deduction at a higher rate. In the Senate FVD voted against both the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting and the novelle.

FVD.title: Tax burden on income and work
FVD.position: FVD's manifesto proposes a 20% flat tax on box 1 income, a tax-free threshold of EUR 30,000 for workers and pensioners, VAT rates of 6% and 19%, no VAT on business-to-business transactions and a phased abolition of the 30% ruling so that expats pay as much tax as Dutch people.

ChristenUnie.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
ChristenUnie.position: Wants fast and fair procedures, stable small-scale reception and fair distribution; the Spreidingswet should stay. It commits to the EU Pact with human-rights safeguards but its Senate group voted against the Dutch implementation act because of the added national measures, and against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet. It opposes criminalising illegal stay and wants rooted children to receive a right of residence, while favouring registration of asylum applications outside Europe.

ChristenUnie.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
ChristenUnie.position: Voted against both the February 2026 bill and the amending bill. Asked the cabinet to follow the Council of State and move in one step in 2030, and said the minister missed a chance for better funding through gift tax. Its amendment allowing a cost deduction for real estate under the rebuttal scheme was adopted. Supported the 2027 Tax Plan including the two box 3 rates.

ChristenUnie.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
ChristenUnie.position: ChristenUnie wants 100,000 new homes a year, at least two-thirds affordable including 30% social rent, a levy on land-value gains ('planbatenheffing') and 20 billion euros extra over the coming decade. It supports phasing out the mortgage interest deduction over at least fifteen years. In the Senate it voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

ChristenUnie.title: Tax burden on income and work
ChristenUnie.position: The manifesto proposes replacing the allowance system with a simple basic credit that does not depend on income and a payable tax credit, and criticises the size of the labour tax credit. ChristenUnie MP Grinwis was first signatory of two amendments adopted on 12 November 2026 that lower the first two box 1 rates and keep the elderly tax credit intact, and the party voted for the amended Tax Plan.

SP.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
SP.position: Says people fleeing war and violence should be received humanely while those with no claim must return as quickly as possible, and wants a net migration ceiling of 40,000 achieved mainly by cutting labour, knowledge and study migration. It wants refugees housed more often in rich municipalities. The SP voted against repealing the Spreidingswet; its Senate group voted against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet and the Pact implementation act, calling the refusal of transitional rules inhumane.

SP.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
SP.position: Voted for the February 2026 bill and against the amending bill. In the Senate the SP voted against the motion stating no objection to withdrawing the original bill. The SP is not among the groups that filed written questions on the amending bill.

SP.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
SP.position: SP wants rents to go down, more social rental homes, a separate ministry and a national building plan. It wants to guarantee the mortgage interest deduction for homes up to 600,000 euros and phase it out faster above that. SP MP Beckerman questioned the minister in April 2026 about investors selling rental homes. In the Senate SP voted against the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

SP.title: Tax burden on income and work
SP.position: The SP manifesto says it will lower income tax substantially and cut VAT on basic products, raise tax on income from capital to the level of income tax, and introduce a 5% millionaires' tax on wealth above EUR 5 million. SP MPs submitted amendments to reverse the narrowing of the healthcare cost deduction and to raise the high corporate tax rate; an SP motion against funding defence through the disability fund contribution was supported by all opposition parties. The SP is not among the groups reported as supporting the Tax Plan.

PvdD.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
PvdD.position: Voted against repealing the Spreidingswet in the House. In the Senate the Volt senator spoke partly on behalf of the PvdD against the Schoof-cabinet bills, and PvdD senators voted against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet and the Pact implementation act; Senator Koffeman said the implementation act carries the spirit of former minister Faber.

PvdD.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
PvdD.position: Voted for the February 2026 bill and against the amending bill. Supported the 2027 Tax Plan, including the two box 3 rates; NOS reports the party was persuaded shortly before the vote in exchange for commitments on other subjects.

PvdD.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
PvdD.position: According to NOS, the PvdD's 2025 manifesto wants to end the mortgage interest deduction for homes above the NHG purchase limit. In the Senate the PvdD voted against the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting and the novelle. The party's own housing page could not be opened for this file.

PvdD.title: Tax burden on income and work
PvdD.position: The manifesto says income tax will be made fairer with a lower low rate, wants 0% VAT on vegetables, fruit, grains, pulses and nuts, lower VAT on repairs and an end to the reduced VAT rate on ornamental plants. PvdD MP Teunissen submitted a series of amendments; the one adding EUR 100 to the flight tax for private jets from 2030 was adopted. IamExpat, citing NOS, reports the party first opposed the Tax Plan but voted for it after commitments on private jets and train fares.

SGP.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
SGP.position: Voted for repealing the Spreidingswet in the House (23 June 2026). In the Senate the SGP saw the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet as a means to gain control but voted against it once the novelle protecting people who help undocumented migrants was rejected; it voted for the Pact implementation act. It asks for better IND assessment of persecuted Christians.

SGP.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
SGP.position: Voted against the February 2026 bill and for the amending bill, which it calls a step in the right direction, and wants all assets under a capital gains tax as soon as possible. Its senator Schalk tabled the rejected Senate motion on withdrawing the original bill. Its amendment to defer tax on leased farmland passed on by inheritance or gift was rejected; its motion asking for a further inventory of improvements was adopted. NOS reported that SGP and JA21 called lowering the tax-free thresholds unacceptable.

SGP.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
SGP.position: According to NOS, the SGP does not want to abolish the mortgage interest deduction but 'is not opposed to a revision'. In the Senate the SGP voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting. No further SGP housing text was verified for this file.

SGP.title: Tax burden on income and work
SGP.position: The SGP manifesto states that the burden on labour is lowered and that the allowance system must be overhauled. SGP MP Stoffer submitted amendments on the youngtimer company-car rule (adopted) and on keeping the small brewers' excise discount. Taxlive reports SGP acted together with JA21 and BBB during the Tax Plan debate.

BBB.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
BBB.position: Co-initiator of the bill to repeal the Spreidingswet and voted for all repeal motions. Its Senate group voted for the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet and the Pact implementation act, saying temporary protection must actually be temporary. MP Vermeer asked that crime and nuisance figures be published per reception location.

BBB.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
BBB.position: Voted against the February 2026 bill and for the amending bill, which it says brings taxation closer to gains actually realised. MP Vermeer objected that the amending bill departs from the usual budget rules. In the Senate, BBB senator Kroon criticised the handling of a bill the cabinet itself intended to change and tabled a motion on a capital gains-based law.

BBB.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
BBB.position: BBB's 2025 manifesto says the mortgage interest deduction should not be limited further, according to NOS. BBB supplied the housing minister, Keijzer, in the previous cabinet; she introduced the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting and the bill to end priority for status holders, and proposed loosening the Wet betaalbare huur. In the Senate BBB voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

BBB.title: Tax burden on income and work
BBB.position: BBB's manifesto calls the tax and allowance system needlessly complex, wants fixed amounts as an allowance instead of complex schemes, a simpler tax on labour, and no increase in taxes on savings (box 3) or enterprise (box 2). BBB MP Vermeer submitted an amendment for further cuts in fuel excise and a motion to scrap the VAT increase on ornamental horticulture for good.

DENK.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
DENK.position: Voted against all motions to repeal the Spreidingswet or to end the duty on municipalities, and for the motions on spreading good practices and on using state property for long-term reception (23 June 2026).

DENK.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
DENK.position: Voted against both the February 2026 bill and the amending bill, and for the adopted cost deduction amendment. Supported the 2027 Tax Plan including the two box 3 rates. MP Ergin called it unacceptable that the minister worked with Groep Markuszower to win support.

DENK.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
DENK.position: According to NOS, DENK's 2025 manifesto wants to end the mortgage interest deduction 'for rich property owners', meaning homes above 500,000 euros. No further DENK housing text was verified for this file.

DENK.title: Tax burden on income and work
DENK.position: DENK's manifesto wants the allowance system replaced, no VAT on fruit and vegetables, lower VAT generally, and a fairer distribution within income tax by asking more of the very rich. DENK MP Ergin filed motions to lower taxes on fuel and on groceries. DENK voted for the amended Tax Plan.

50PLUS.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
50PLUS.position: Voted against repealing the Spreidingswet but for a motion asking the government to formulate concrete conditions for repeal. Its senator voted for the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet, criticising D66 for not doing so, and for the Pact implementation act.

50PLUS.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
50PLUS.position: Voted against the February 2026 bill and for the amending bill. MP Van Brenk said signals from implementing bodies must be heeded and the amending bill should take effect later if they have too little time; the group asked how capital flight is monitored. Supported the 2027 Tax Plan according to the reported vote.

50PLUS.title: Tax burden on income and work
50PLUS.position: The 50PLUS manifesto calls for full application of the statutory inflation correction in income tax. MP Van Brenk co-signed the adopted Grinwis/Van Brenk amendment lowering tax on work, and leader Jan Struijs questioned in the debate whether people with only a state pension benefit from the first-bracket cut. 50PLUS voted for the amended Tax Plan.

Volt.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
Volt.position: Wants a humane, common European refugee policy with redistribution between member states, and an end to internal border checks. Voted against repealing the Spreidingswet; in the Senate it requested roll-call votes and voted against all three Schoof-cabinet bills and against the Pact implementation act.

Volt.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
Volt.position: Voted for the February 2026 bill and against the amending bill. MP Dassen described the amending bill as a gift to people in box 2 at the expense of future generations. Co-proposer with PRO of the adopted Tax Plan amendment creating two box 3 rates.

Volt.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
Volt.position: According to NOS, Volt wants to phase out the mortgage interest deduction 'as soon as possible'. In the Senate Volt voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

Volt.title: Tax burden on income and work
Volt.position: Volt's manifesto proposes more box 1 brackets combined with a basic income, and aligning expat rulings between EU member states. Volt's Dassen co-submitted the adopted tax-shift amendment with PRO's Klaver, and Volt voted for the amended Tax Plan.

Lid Keijzer.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
Lid Keijzer.position: Voted for the amending bill and for the rejected amendment to lower the box 3 rate by 3 percentage points. Said in the plenary debate that the current box 3 tax drives entrepreneurs out of the country and argued for a tax that those who pay it experience as fair.
